coverageNote: Enumeration matched the expectation exactly: 9 units (the domain directory itself plus 11.01-11.08) and 52 files. The domain-directory unit carries music-licensing-index.md, music-licensing-cx.md and the three flat leaf features 11.09/11.10/11.11. All 52 files were processed. Large files (7 files between 46KB and 59KB) were read section-by-section in the sandbox rather than raw: for every file the Overview, Role Lens, Behavior (and its custom sub-sections), Happy Path, Edge Cases / Failure Modes, States, Decisions and Cross-Cut Map/Details sections were read in full with line numbers. Deep Think Annotations and Cross-Cut Notes were read selectively (they are rationale/pointer sections, and every ratified rule they carry is restated in a Decisions row). All 168 Open Questions rows across the domain were parsed programmatically for owner + deferral target (0 malformed on that test); the text of Open Questions rows was read in full for the domain index, all 8 sub-domain indexes, and every file where a finding candidate touched a tracked question. Rubric dimensions 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 were scored N/A for every unit: problem statement, personas, constraints, success metrics and competitive landscape are authored in meta/ and ideation-index.md and are referenced-never-redefined here (an explicit convention, e.g. music-licensing-index.md:62 'Personas from meta/personas.md (D-19). Referenced, never redefined.'). Dimensions 3, 7 and 8 were scored for all 9 units, giving 3 applicable checkpoints per unit and 27 in total. Devil's-advocate pass dropped 6 candidate findings that did not survive: (a) 11.01.04's self-declared Role-Lens-vs-CX-03 contradiction about holder identity is explicitly tracked at 11.01.04 Q-02 with owner User and target /create-prd; (b) music-licensing-cx.md CX-16's 'correction owed' on 11.04.01's key-space claim is in fact written down at 11.04.02:66-70 and D-09; (c) 11.05-cx CX-03 Q5's PENDING on interpolation chains/cycles is answered by 11.05.04's 'Interpolation of an interpolation' edge case and 11.02.03's Traversal invariant; (d) 11.01-cx CX-05 Q2's PENDING on whether a one-sided hold releases automatically is answered by 11.01.04's 'One side accepts, the other declines' edge case; (e) 11.04-cx CX-01 Q4's PENDING on disclosing the vetoing party to the buyer is answered by 11.02.01 D-11 and 11.04.02 D-06; (f) 11.07.02's edge-case PENDING on manifest-vs-current-split is properly tracked at 11.07.02 Q-04 (owner Agent, target /create-prd-architecture) and cross-referenced correctly from 11.07.03. Latency and rate-limit gaps were not reported: the domain index's 'Not-Product Concerns Routed Out' table routes clearance-graph traversal performance to /create-prd-compile and catalogue enumeration defence to /create-prd-security, and every file's latency language cites those routings.

findings.short_summary: Verdict has no input for a missing sample declaration
findings.claim: Three files make an affirmative 'nothing borrowed' sample declaration a precondition of one-stop status, but 11.02.01 — the file that owns the verdict computation and derives the one-stop boolean — has no declaration-presence input, no verdict value for its absence, and a one-stop rule that omits it entirely. An implementer building the gate from 11.02.01 ships one-stop on undeclared works; an implementer building it from 11.02.03/11.05.01 does not. The verdict value an undeclared-but-otherwise-clean work should receive is not specified anywhere.
findings.evidence: 11.02.01-clearance-computation-one-stop.md:49-57 enumerates the verdict's inputs exhaustively — 'The verdict is a function of five inputs: 1. The consent graph (domain 09) ... 2. The completeness attestation (11.02.02) ... 3. The encumbrance set (11.02.03) — is anything upstream tainted, walked through the derivation graph 4. The effective work policy (11.04.03) ... 5. The required rights sides (D-06)' — declaration presence is not among them. 11.02.01:68 defines the only candidate verdict narrowly: '`incomplete` | The record is not closed — shares do not sum, or no valid completeness attestation exists'. 11.02.01:79-82 fixes the one-stop rule with no declaration term: '**`one-stop` is not a verdict.** It is a separate derived boolean, true only when the combined verdict is `clearable-now` **and** the buyer transacts with exactly one counterparty (D-10, DT-06).' 11.02.01:92 step 4 checks only 'no encumbrance in this work or any ancestor (11.02.03)', which an undeclared work passes vacuously. Against that: 11.02.03-encumbrance-declaration.md:207 D-02 'Silence is not cleanliness — an undeclared work is not one-stop'; 11.02.03:126 'Nobody declares anything — silence | **Silence must not mean clean.** A work with no declaration and no attestation is not one-stop'; 11.02.03:158 States/Empty '"Nothing declared" — not "clean". The distinction is the entire feature.'; and 11.05.01-sample-declaration-identification.md:187 States 'Empty — negative | Asked, answered "nothing borrowed" | **A different state from the above**, and only this one can support one-stop via 11.02.02', restated at 11.05.01:238 D-05 '"Nothing borrowed" is an attributed assertion — which is what makes never-asked and asked-and-said-no different states, and only the latter can support one-stop (11.02.02)'. The sub-domain's own CX file records the question as unresolved and routes it to a stage that has already completed: 11.02-clearance-one-stop-status-cx.md:82 '5. **State transition conflict**: `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` — whether a work can be one-stop with attestation but no encumbrance declaration (i.e. is silence on sampling equivalent to "no samples"?). **Silence must not mean clean.** Provisional: both required.'
findings.failure_scenario: A solo writer-producer uploads a work, closes the session, attests both party lists complete, sets a permissive policy, and never answers the sample-declaration prompt. Implementer A builds 11.02.01 literally: all five enumerated inputs pass (shares close, valid attestation exists, the encumbrance set is empty, policy permits, both sides derived), so the combined verdict is `clearable-now`; counterparty count is 1; the derived boolean fires and the work is badged and sold as one-stop. Implementer B builds 11.02.03 D-02 and 11.05.01 D-05 literally: no affirmative 'nothing borrowed' declaration exists, so the work is withheld from one-stop. The two systems disagree on the domain's flagship signal for the most common cold-start case in the catalogue, and A sells a one-stop licence on a work whose sample content was never asserted — exactly the false positive 11.02.01 D-02 and domain D-09 exist to prevent.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether declaration presence is a sixth verdict input; if so, which verdict value its absence yields (extend `incomplete`, add a new state, or gate only the derived one-stop boolean); and whether the gate refuses issuance on an undeclared work or only withholds the badge.

findings.claim: 11.02.01 D-10 ratifies that the one-stop badge is displayed only when the buyer transacts with exactly one counterparty, and its edge-case table applies that rule explicitly to a many-writer work. 11.02.02 specifies the buyer-facing string as 'One-stop' on works with 3 and 4 named rights holders, four separate times, with no marker on either side. Both statements cannot hold: a work with four distinct listed parties is four counterparties, which D-10 forbids badging as one-stop.
findings.evidence: 11.02.01-clearance-computation-one-stop.md:196 D-10 states the rule and its reason: '**"One-stop" is displayed only when the buyer transacts with exactly one counterparty.** Otherwise the verdict reads `clearable-now` with the counterparty count stated. Multi-hyphenates count once. | Per DT-06 — one-stop is an industry term of art meaning one signature, not one clean record. The platform does not redefine a term of art in its own favour; a supervisor who filters on the badge and gets fourteen counterparties has been lied to.' Applied at 11.02.01:108: 'Work has 14 co-writers, all on-platform, all attested, all policy-permitted | `clearable-now`, **14 counterparties**. Not displayed as one-stop (D-10).' Contradicted by 11.02.02-catalogue-completeness-attestation.md:85-87: '`One-stop — attested by 1 of 4 named parties, reconstructed` and `One-stop — captured at session, confirmed by 4 of 4` are both true statements about clearable works and they carry very different risk.'; 11.02.02:121 Happy Path step 7 'the work can become one-stop for scopes that permit it, rendered with grade and corroboration: `One-stop — captured at session, confirmed by 3 of 3`'; 11.02.02:128 'Buyer: "One-stop — attested by 1 of 4 named parties, reconstructed."'; 11.02.02:136 'One-stop — attested by Alice, confirmed by 2 of 4. Ray Dolan (deceased) — share held by estate, not confirmed.' The denominator is defined as distinct humans, not stakes, at 11.02.02:83: 'Corroboration | Integer: count of **distinct verified human identities** (D-07) other than the attester who have corroborated, over the count of distinct human identities on the attested list' — so '4 named parties' is four counterparties under D-10's own counting rule, and 11.02.02:138's genuinely single-party case is written differently ('One-stop — sole rights holder, self-attested'), confirming the multi-party strings are not an entity/administrator special case. Neither file carries a marker, a deferral, or a cross-reference reconciling the two; 11.02.01 is dated 2026-07-23 and 11.02.02 is dated 2026-07-16.
findings.failure_scenario: A four-writer work is fully attested (1 of 4 corroborated), unencumbered and policy-permitted for a podcast sync. The buyer-facing badge is built from 11.02.02's specified strings and renders 'One-stop — attested by 1 of 4 named parties, reconstructed'. A music supervisor filters the catalogue on one-stop, shortlists it under a Friday deadline, and discovers at quote time that four separate counterparties must each execute — the precise harm 11.02.01 D-10 was ratified to prevent ('a supervisor who filters on the badge and gets fourteen counterparties has been lied to'). Built from 11.02.01 instead, the same work renders 'Clearable now — 4 rights holders' and never enters the one-stop filter, so the two specs produce different search result sets for the domain's flagship filter.

findings.short_summary: Hold response deadline and expiry warning lead are literal N
findings.claim: 11.01.04 specifies two time-triggered behaviours without values and with no tracked question covering either: the deadline at which an unanswered second-side hold request expires, and the lead time at which the buyer is warned before a hold lapses. The warning lead is written as a literal unfilled placeholder ('T-minus-N'). The domain fixes comparable numbers everywhere else, so the omission is a gap rather than a deliberate deferral.
findings.evidence: 11.01.04-holds-exclusivity-windows.md:53 'Second side never responds | Hold request expires unaccepted at a deadline; does not linger as a phantom | Buyer: "No response from the publishing side — treat as unavailable"' — the deadline is named but never valued. 11.01.04:54 'Buyer's client goes quiet; hold lapses mid-edit | Expiry fires; buyer warned before, not after | Warning at T-minus-N; on lapse: "Your hold expired. Re-request?" — never silent' — N is a literal placeholder. 11.01.04:92 D-02 makes the warning normative without a value: 'Hold expiry is automatic and warns the owner as well as the buyer'. The file's three Open Questions (11.01.04:99-101) cover different axes and none covers either number: Q-01 'Are holds free?', Q-02 'Is the holding buyer's identity visible to the owner?', Q-03 'What is the maximum hold window, and can it be extended indefinitely?' — Q-03 is explicitly scoped as 'a market-design ceiling rather than an engineering threshold' about the window's maximum, not about warning lead or solicitation timeout. Sibling features do fix these numbers: 11.02.04-multi-party-consent-routing.md:60 'Request expires at a **fixed window** (default 14 days, chase reminders at day 3 and day 7)'; 11.02.03-encumbrance-declaration.md:133 '90 / 30 / 7 days out: "Your clearance for [source] ends [date]"'; 11.04.02-co-owner-veto-approval.md:103 'the owner is notified 7 days before and on the day'; music-licensing-cx.md:176 'term reaches T-90/T-30/T-7 → warn owner'.
findings.failure_scenario: A buyer places an exclusive hold; the master side accepts and the publishing side does not respond. Implementer A picks 14 days for the solicitation timeout (copying 11.02.04's default) and warns the buyer 7 days before lapse; implementer B picks 72 hours and 24 hours respectively on the grounds that a hold is a fast browse-stage action. Under A a buyer under a three-week air date waits two weeks for a phantom hold to die; under B a buyer cutting an edit gets one day's notice before the work they are cutting to becomes available to a competitor. Both are consistent with the text, and the domain-wide P-01 requirement ('perishable state must warn its owner, not only its counterparty') is satisfiable by both.
findings.forcedInvention: The hold-request response deadline for the second rights side, and the pre-expiry warning lead time (the literal 'N' in 'T-minus-N') for both buyer and owner.

findings.short_summary: Licence expiry warning lead time is a literal N
findings.claim: 11.08.04 makes pre-expiry warning to both buyer and owner a ratified decision but leaves the lead time as an unfilled placeholder, and no Open Question in the file or the sub-domain index covers it. The sub-domain therefore cannot say when a licence-expiry warning fires, while three sibling features fix their own cadences precisely.
findings.evidence: 11.08.04-licence-amendment-expiry-lifecycle.md:58 'Term expires while the use is live | Use becomes unlicensed. **The buyer must be warned well before**, not at the moment. | Warning at T-minus-N to both sides; expiry is not a surprise' — N is a literal placeholder. Made normative without a value at 11.08.04:34-36 'Automatic, unattended, and it must warn **both** sides: the buyer (their use is about to become unlicensed) and the owner (a renewal is a sale they will otherwise miss)' and 11.08.04:103 D-03 'Expiry warns the owner as well as the buyer | Per DT-02 — an unattended expiry is a sale the seller never knew about'. The file's Open Questions (11.08.04:111-113) are Q-01 remedy for a licence that should never have issued, Q-02 whether 'the old record always survives' is a platform invariant, Q-03 whether a licence may be amended to narrow scope — none covers the warning cadence; nor do the sub-domain index's Q-01/Q-02/Q-03 (11.08-licence-instrument-lifecycle-index.md:75-77: legal status of the instrument, DDEX-vs-native grammar, public-vs-authenticated verification). Comparable cadences are fixed elsewhere: 11.02.03-encumbrance-declaration.md:200 'pre-expiry warnings at 90/30/7 days'; 11.04.02-co-owner-veto-approval.md:103 'notified 7 days before and on the day'; music-licensing-cx.md:235 'a lapsing clearance re-encumbers a work with no user action; warn at 90/30/7 days'.
findings.failure_scenario: A 3-year sync licence approaches expiry on a campaign still running. Implementer A adopts the domain's clearance-lapse cadence (90/30/7) and the owner gets three months to sell a renewal; implementer B warns at 7 days, which is inside a typical brand's procurement cycle, so the renewal 'sale the seller never knew about' that D-03 exists to prevent happens anyway and the buyer's use silently becomes unlicensed mid-campaign. Both implementations satisfy every written sentence in 11.08.04.
findings.forcedInvention: The pre-expiry warning schedule for an issued licence (the literal 'N' in 'T-minus-N'), for both the buyer and the rights holder.

findings.short_summary: Grand rights must be blockable but have no key space
findings.claim: 11.11 requires that grand rights exist as a refusable category and never auto-approve, and simultaneously forbids representing them in the scope grammar. 11.04.02 D-09 fixes that category blocks key on the scope grammar and 11.04.01 enumerates its auto-approve eligibility bars without a grand-rights bar. The three statements cannot all hold: there is no key space in which the required category can be authored, and no enforcement point for the required exclusion.
findings.evidence: 11.11-grand-rights-dramatic-performance.md:89 D-01 makes the category's existence the node's entire purpose: 'The node exists even though the product is `won't` | Per DT-01 — without the category, auto-approve policy has nothing to exclude and can silently grant dramatic rights'. 11.11:90 D-02 'Grand rights are never auto-approvable | No writer ticking "auto-approve under £500" means "you may stage a musical"', restated as an edge case at 11.11:53 'Auto-approve policy set on the work | **Must not apply.** No writer means "auto-approve a musical" when they tick "auto-approve film". | Grand rights must be excluded from any auto-approve default, or the policy silently grants something enormous'. But 11.11:91 D-03 removes the representation: 'Not modelled as a scope-grammar media value | Per DT-02 — treatment approval is not expressible as scope, and pretending otherwise makes it quotable', reinforced at music-licensing-cx.md:288 R-05 'Rejected (11.11 DT-02) ... Adding it as a media axis value would let the system auto-approve a licence whose defining term it cannot represent. The one licence type not reducible to scope.' The grammar's Media axis has no dramatic/theatrical value — 11.08.01-licence-scope-grammar.md:47 'Media | podcast · film · TV · advertising · game · social/UGC · radio · in-store · trailer-house reels · physical release' — and 11.04.02-co-owner-veto-approval.md:240 D-09 fixes where a category block can live: '**Two key spaces**: category blocks key on the scope grammar and take effect at authoring time, catalogue-wide; buyer blocks key on party identity'. 11.04.01-per-work-licensing-policy.md:38 enumerates the auto-approve bars closed — 'Auto-approve eligibility bars — exclusivity, self-dealing, MFN, dormancy, dispute (D-05..D-09, D-15)' — with no grand-rights bar in D-05, D-07, D-08, D-09 or D-15. 11.11 Q-02 is recorded RESOLVED (11.11:99) and resolves only the treatment-approval term as instrument payload per 11.08.01 D-13; it does not supply a category key space.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer builds 11.04.02's block authoring UI from D-09 (category blocks key on the scope grammar) and finds no value for dramatic use, so no 'never a musical' block can be authored — 11.11 D-01's stated purpose for the node is unbuildable. A theatre then requests dramatic use through 11.03.02; the request form must resolve to a point in the grammar (11.08.01 D-04: an unset axis returns No; 11.02.01 D-14: no scope, no verdict), so the implementer either adds a media value — which 11.11 D-03 and R-05 forbid, and which reintroduces exactly the auto-approve hazard those decisions exist to close — or the request is declared under 'film', where a writer's standing 'auto-approve film under £500' policy passes it, and the policy 'silently grants something enormous' precisely as 11.11:53 warns.

findings.short_summary: Domain CX asserts contradictions its children already resolved
findings.claim: The domain cross-cut file asserts, in the present tense and as live routed work, two contradictions that the [DEEP] child files have since resolved, and one of the two is additionally attributed to the wrong file. A reader of the domain CX — which is the file the pattern section explicitly nominates for platform-level escalation — is directed to unify a consent engine that 11.04.02 D-12 already unified, and to expect a contradiction in 11.04.01 that 11.04.02 already corrected.
findings.evidence: music-licensing-cx.md:6 dates the file '**Last updated**: 2026-07-18' while claiming post-deepening currency at :5 'Status: [DEEP] — 8 sub-domains + 3 features; intra-domain cross-cuts mapped and synthesised after the deepening pass.' It then asserts at :274-276 'Two files (11.04.01 and 11.07.01) **currently** describe the same engine with contradictory defaults. **The consent engine must be unified with an explicit per-category default, or the platform ships two block systems that will eventually disagree about refusal.** Routed to `/create-prd-architecture`.' — with the permissive default attributed to 11.04.01, which specifies no block defaults at all (its Behavior at 11.04.01:30-33 covers policy key space and per-work overrides only). The unification it demands is already ratified in the file that does own block defaults, dated 2026-07-23: 11.04.02-co-owner-veto-approval.md:243 D-12 '**The block table's default is empty/permissive — except AI training, which defaults to refused** | 11.07 D-03 (opt-in, never opt-out) inverts this feature's default for exactly one category. The mechanism is shared; the default is not.', stated in prose at 11.04.02:77-81 '**One category inverts this.** AI training defaults to **refused** ... An implementer who reads "permissive default" and applies it uniformly ships the single most damaging bug available in this domain', and rendered as a state at 11.04.02:182 'Except AI training, which reads "Refused" with nothing set (D-12, 11.07 D-03)'. Second instance: music-licensing-cx.md:27 CX-16 '**Contradiction / correction owed**: the grammar's six axes carry NO counterparty axis, so buyer blocks live *outside* the grammar. 11.04.01's claim "the policy key space is the scope grammar" is true for category blocks, false for buyer blocks', amplified at :148-149 'This is a correction owed on the 11.04.01 text, not a design gap — but it must be written down or two files contradict.' The correction is written down, in 11.04.02:66-70: '11.04.01 states the policy key space *is* the scope grammar — true for categories, false for buyers. The grammar has no counterparty axis, so a buyer block cannot fold into an effective work policy the way a category block does'. Neither CX row carries an owner or a resolution marker.
findings.failure_scenario: At /create-prd-architecture an architect reads P-04 as a live requirement and designs a unification of the block engine with a new per-category default table, unaware that 11.04.02 D-12 already fixes the exact rule (permissive everywhere, refused for AI training) — producing either duplicate machinery or a second, competing statement of a default whose divergence D-12 calls 'the single most damaging bug available in this domain'. Separately, a spec writer reading CX-16 edits 11.04.01's Behavior to carve out buyer blocks, creating a third statement of the two-key-space rule that must then be kept in sync with 11.04.02 D-09 and 11.04.03's fold.

findings.short_summary: Edge case deferred to a workflow stage that already ran
findings.claim: 11.07.03 leaves an enumerated edge case with no behaviour and defers it to `/ideate-discover Step 5 deepening` — a stage that has already completed for this domain — with no owner and no substitute question in the file's Open Questions. The tracking is malformed: the deferral target cannot ever consume it, so the row is an untracked gap wearing a tracked marker.
findings.evidence: 11.07.03-training-compensation-attribution.md:57 'Rights holder wants attribution but not money | Plausible and unsupported by a payment-shaped feature | `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`' — the What-Happens cell states no behaviour, the marker names no owner, and the named stage has run: music-licensing-cx.md:5 records the domain CX as '[DEEP] ... mapped and synthesised **after the deepening pass**', 11.07.01-ai-training-consent-opt-out.md:109 records a Step 5 resolution as historical ('Resolved `/ideate-discover` Step 5, 2026-07-17'), and 11.03.01-rate-cards-pricing-rules.md:100 states it outright: 'Deferral expired — `/ideate-discover` Step 5 has run and did not answer it.' 11.07.03's own Open Questions do not cover it — the file's rows are Q-01 (division basis), Q-02 (stems vs mixes weighting) and the manifest-vs-current-split question, which is correctly tracked as 11.07.02 Q-04 (11.07.02-corpus-assembly-dataset-deals.md:105, owner Agent, target /create-prd-architecture). Compare the same file's well-formed handling of an adjacent gap at 11.07.03:52 'Splits changed since the manifest pinned | Follow the manifest or the current split? Consistency with 11.02.01 argues current. | 11.07.02 Q-04 — unresolved'.
findings.failure_scenario: A rights holder consents to corpus inclusion and asks to be credited in the manifest but to waive their share of the deal value. Implementer A treats the waiver as unsupported and pays them anyway (the row says the feature is 'payment-shaped'), leaving an unwanted disbursement and an accrued balance under D-04's 'sub-minimum payouts accrue rather than vanish'. Implementer B builds an attribution-only consent state, which changes 11.07.02's manifest schema and 11.07.03's division denominator. Nothing in the tree adjudicates, and no downstream stage will ever be handed the question, because the stage it points at has already run.

findings.short_summary: Sub-domain CX defers a live rule to a completed stage
findings.claim: The sub-domain's cross-cut file records the declaration-vs-attestation precondition question as `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` with a provisional answer, no owner, and a deferral target that has already been consumed. The question is the one behind finding #001; because the marker points at a completed stage and names no owner, no later stage will receive it.
findings.evidence: 11.02-clearance-one-stop-status-cx.md:82 '5. **State transition conflict**: `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` — whether a work can be one-stop with attestation but no encumbrance declaration (i.e. is silence on sampling equivalent to "no samples"?). **Silence must not mean clean.** Provisional: both required.' The stage named has completed — the three children of this very sub-domain are `[DEEP]` (11.02-clearance-one-stop-status-index.md:29-31 lists 11.02.01, 11.02.02 and 11.02.03 as `[DEEP]` with 14, 11 and 11 hypotheses), and 11.03.01-rate-cards-pricing-rules.md:100 states the general fact: 'Deferral expired — `/ideate-discover` Step 5 has run and did not answer it.' The row carries no owner, unlike every one of the 168 Open Questions rows in this domain, all of which pair an owner with a live deferral target (e.g. 11.02-clearance-one-stop-status-index.md:73 'Q-01 | ... | User | `/create-prd-security` (legal escalation)'). The provisional answer it carries ('both required') is also the one 11.02.01 does not implement — see finding 11-music-licensing#001.
findings.failure_scenario: A remediation or PRD pass sweeps the tree for open decisions by reading Open Questions tables and owner-tagged markers. This row is in neither: it lives inside a CX synthesis answer, names no owner, and points at a stage that has already run. The one-stop precondition therefore stays unratified indefinitely, and the divergence between 11.02.01's verdict algorithm and 11.02.03 D-02 / 11.05.01 D-05 reaches /write-architecture-spec unresolved, where an IA author picks one reading silently.
